meta.title: Thai A2 Elementary
meta.subtitle: 750 words · both directions, as two cards per word
meta.desc: Both study directions in one deck: Thai → English (see the Thai, recall the meaning) and English → Thai (see an English meaning, recall the Thai). Each direction is a card of its own with its own schedule, so recognising a word and producing it are learnt separately. 750 words for an elementary learner, aligned to A2 of the Common European Framework of Reference, whose global descriptor begins 'Can understand sentences and frequently used expressions related to areas of most immediate relevance' — a learner here is able to manage simple, routine exchanges of information on familiar matters — personal and family information, shopping, the local area, work — and to describe in simple terms their background, their surroundings and what they immediately need. The words already taught by the levels below this one are left out. WHERE THESE WORDS COME FROM, since it matters: no exam board publishes a graded word list for Thai, so this deck is not any examination's vocabulary and does not claim to be. It is assembled from two things that can be stated. 508 of the 750 come from a vocabulary written for the level's scope — relatives and the people around you, jobs, work and study, clothes and shopping, more food, cooking and eating out, the furniture of a home, the town and its buildings, travel and directions, the countryside, nature and animals, the seasons and the points of the compass, health and the body, feelings and character, free time, sport and festivals, more classifiers, telling what happened and when, comparing and giving an opinion, and the everyday verbs of moving, dressing and doing — and the other 242 are the commonest remaining words of Thai, taken from the word counts of the Thai National Corpus, a large collection of written Thai. The cards are dealt by that frequency, so the words you meet most often come first. Every headword is printed in Thai script with a romanisation beneath it in the Paiboon system, which marks the TONE on every syllable — no mark for mid, à low, â falling, á high, ǎ rising — because a Thai word said on the wrong tone is a different word; the Thai Alphabet deck, the first in this collection, teaches the script and the rules that decide a tone. 124 nouns show the classifier they are counted with (a house is counted in หลัง, an animal in ตัว), and there are no forms to learn: Thai words never change shape. Example sentences come with 599 of the 750 words, three apiece for 375 of them, with the word picked out in colour and a speaker beside the sentence and the headword. Sources. Level: the Common European Framework of Reference (Council of Europe), global scale. Meanings, romanisation, classifiers and some example sentences: English Wiktionary, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0). Frequency: the Thai National Corpus word list as distributed by PyThaiNLP (CC0). Example sentences: Tatoeba (tatoeba.org), CC BY 2.0 FR.
